candidate_classes_tested.basis: Pedestrian exposure engages vehicle safety; it does not establish a separate human-facing AI support interaction with developmental, consent-impairment or harmful-dependency signals under this class. Injury does not identify nonactivation of a protective control.
candidate_classes_tested.failure_test: The independent context/person/time duty, sufficiently visible heightened-risk signals and materially omitted bounded response are not established together.
candidate_classes_tested.success_test: Ordinary repair, refusal, seizure or human recovery is not evidence of an engaged heightened personal-protection duty being discharged by the AI.
candidate_classes_tested.exclusions_test: Neither adverse consequences nor commercial dependency establish personal vulnerability. No available-control nonactivation is inferred from absence of protection.

taxonomy_review.notes: Current class set reviewed. Prior roles and unclassified/candidate dispositions preserved. New relational/protection classes do not replace ordinary identity, consent, scope, service-floor or event/audit integrity mechanisms.

taxonomy_mapping_dispositions.reason: Cruise's initial mandatory crash reports omitted the materially relevant post-crash dragging behaviour. The required regulatory reporting artefact therefore presented a truncated account of the captured occurrence, degrading audit-evidence integrity before NHTSA review.

The post-crash dragging event was captured in other evidence and was later identifiable; the failure was its omission from the required regulatory report rather than complete non-capture of the event.
NHTSA was ultimately able to reconstruct the omitted dragging behaviour sufficiently to make a regulatory finding, so the audit trail was not rendered non-reconstructable.

new_assessment.coverage_note: All twelve dimensions reviewed. The driverless vehicle’s post-impact movement and roughly twenty-foot dragging materially contributed to a medically significant injury occurrence. Professional treatment supports retained S3. The human-driven first impact remains separate; the record does not allocate life-threatening or permanent injury to the later movement sufficiently for a higher band. Missing later clinical follow-up does not erase actual injury. Relational-role and heightened personal-protection recognition and exclusions independently tested.
